new_exact_v1_reviews.title: LAWS: Learning from Actual Workloads Symbolically -- A Self-Certifying Parametrized Cache Architecture for Neural Inference, Robotics, and Edge Deployment
new_exact_v1_reviews.problem: We introduce LAWS (Learning from Actual Workloads Symbolically), a self-certifying inference caching architecture that builds a growing library of certified expert functions from deployment observations.
new_exact_v1_reviews.old_path_and_changed_constraint: The fundamental gap: no existing system automatically discovers reusable computational patterns from deployment experience, certifies their validity formally, and grows the library continuously with use.
new_exact_v1_reviews.mechanism_and_ownership: We introduce LAWS (Learning from Actual Workloads Symbolically), a self-certifying inference caching architecture that builds a growing library of certified expert functions from deployment observations.
new_exact_v1_reviews.evaluation_contract: Further results include a monotone hit rate theorem (any-match routing ensures coverage only increases), an expert library growth rate of O(2^H log N) where H is workload entropy, a fleet learning convergence theorem with Omega(K) speedup for K-unit fleets, and an over-the-air update bandwidth bound.
new_exact_v1_reviews.proof_and_nonproof: Evidence is author-reported exact-v1 mechanism/evaluation evidence. It does not establish cross-model, cross-hardware, cross-workload or production generality unless those conditions are explicitly named above.
new_exact_v1_reviews.tradeoffs_and_failure_modes: The fundamental limitation: every piece of knowledge must be hand-authored by a human who understands it.
new_exact_v1_reviews.coexistence_boundary: The older path remains appropriate where its workload and SLO do not trigger the changed constraint; the paper is treated as a conditional branch, not a universal replacement.

new_exact_v1_reviews.title: RetentiveKV: State-Space Memory for Uncertainty-Aware Multimodal KV Cache Eviction
new_exact_v1_reviews.problem: Multimodal Large Language Models face severe challenges in computational efficiency and memory consumption due to the substantial expansion of the visual KV cache when processing long visual contexts.
new_exact_v1_reviews.old_path_and_changed_constraint: Multimodal Large Language Models face severe challenges in computational efficiency and memory consumption due to the substantial expansion of the visual KV cache when processing long visual contexts.
new_exact_v1_reviews.mechanism_and_ownership: To address these challenges, we propose RetentiveKV, an entropy-driven KV cache optimization method that reformulates KV eviction from "discrete context truncation" to "continuous memory evolution" based on State Space Models.
new_exact_v1_reviews.evaluation_contract: Extensive experiments on multimodal benchmarks demonstrate that RetentiveKV achieves 5.0 times KV cache compression and 1.5 times decoding acceleration.
new_exact_v1_reviews.proof_and_nonproof: Evidence is author-reported exact-v1 mechanism/evaluation evidence. It does not establish cross-model, cross-hardware, cross-workload or production generality unless those conditions are explicitly named above.
new_exact_v1_reviews.tradeoffs_and_failure_modes: This mechanism preserves visual tokens exhibiting high uncertainty during early decoding stages and updates them continuously as decoding progresses, all while incurring only O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) memory overhead.
new_exact_v1_reviews.coexistence_boundary: The older path remains appropriate where its workload and SLO do not trigger the changed constraint; the paper is treated as a conditional branch, not a universal replacement.

new_exact_v1_reviews.title: FASQ: Flexible Accelerated Subspace Quantization for Calibration-Free LLM Compression
new_exact_v1_reviews.problem: Compressing large language models (LLMs) for deployment on commodity GPUs remains challenging: conventional scalar quantization is limited to fixed bit-widths (e.g., 8/4/3-bit), offers only a few discrete compression points, and typically requires calibration data.
new_exact_v1_reviews.old_path_and_changed_constraint: Compressing large language models (LLMs) for deployment on commodity GPUs remains challenging: conventional scalar quantization is limited to fixed bit-widths (e.g., 8/4/3-bit), offers only a few discrete compression points, and typically requires calibration data.
new_exact_v1_reviews.mechanism_and_ownership: We present FASQ (Flexible Accelerated Subspace Quantization), a calibration-free framework that applies product quantization to LLM weight matrices.
new_exact_v1_reviews.evaluation_contract: On Meta-Llama-3-8B, FASQ surpasses 4-bit GPTQ and AWQ in accuracy (67.1-67.7 avg.) at 37-42% model size, with consistent results on Qwen3-8B and Qwen3.5-9B-Base.
new_exact_v1_reviews.proof_and_nonproof: Evidence is author-reported exact-v1 mechanism/evaluation evidence. It does not establish cross-model, cross-hardware, cross-workload or production generality unless those conditions are explicitly named above.
new_exact_v1_reviews.tradeoffs_and_failure_modes: FASQ is the only compressed method that accelerates decode beyond FP16, offering calibration-free compression, continuous size–quality trade-offs, and real-time inference on a single consumer GPU.
new_exact_v1_reviews.coexistence_boundary: The older path remains appropriate where its workload and SLO do not trigger the changed constraint; the paper is treated as a conditional branch, not a universal replacement.
